_comment: Runtime routing matrix for rules.txt, driven by harness.py against a real sing-box core running the app-built config.

Outcomes: P = proxy outbound (the SOCKS5 marker on 127.0.0.1:1081 answered), D = direct outbound (an HTTP direct marker answered), R = rejected (SOCKS5 failure reply, or the connection closed/reset before any byte).
Scenarios: s1 = config built with global default TUNNEL (route.final -> proxy tag); s2 = global default DIRECT (route.final -> direct).
`expect` is the baseline for both platforms; `override.<platform>.expect` wins for that platform only and must carry a `note`.

Every test domain resolves (via the hosts DNS server the harness puts in place of the app's DNS servers) to dns_hosts_target. That address is deliberately NOT covered by any rule in rules.txt (the DIRECT CIDR is 192.0.2.128/25), so a domain case's outcome never depends on whether sing-box resolves the destination before matching ip_cidr rules.
Literal-IP direct cases use 192.0.2.200, inside the DIRECT CIDR; the direct marker listens on both addresses (CI binds them to lo).

cases.note: Rule 1 (DOMAIN-SUFFIX example-proxy.test,PROXY). An explicit PROXY rule wins in both scenarios.
Matches rule 1 (PROXY) and rule 3 (DOMAIN-KEYWORD blockme,REJECT). sing-box takes the first matching route rule, so rule order, not specificity, decides: PROXY.
DOMAIN is an exact match, so a subdomain falls through to route.final (S1 proxy, S2 direct).
Fails rule 4's [0-9]+; no other rule matches, so route.final decides.
Literal IPv4, rule 5 (IP-CIDR 198.51.100.0/24,PROXY). The proxy marker never dials out, so the TEST-NET address needs no route.
Literal IPv4, rule 7 (IP-CIDR 192.0.2.128/25,DIRECT); the direct marker listens on 192.0.2.200.

android.note: Android's SingboxConfigBuilder.buildRoute puts {ip_version: 6, action: reject} before every user rule whenever the config is built with enableIpv6Dns=false (the build() default and the app default), so captured IPv6 is refused instead of carried. Rule 8 is therefore unreachable on Android in both scenarios. iOS has no such rule, so rule 8 applies there.

cases.note: Literal IPv6, rule 8 (IP-CIDR6 2001:db8:1::/48,PROXY). Sent to the inbound as SOCKS5 ATYP 4; no IPv6 connectivity is needed because the proxy marker never dials.
Rule 9 (DST-PORT 8443,DIRECT): a port-only rule matches any destination on that port.
Same host on a port rule 9 does not cover; route.final decides.
Rule 10 (GEOSITE openai,DIRECT) through the bundled geosite-openai rule-set (domain_suffix openai.com).
Rule 11 (RULE-SET telegram,REJECT) through the bundled geosite-telegram rule-set.

Literal IP inside rule 7 (DIRECT), but the HTTP Host header is www.example-proxy.test. route.rules[0] is the sniff action, which records the sniffed host as the connection's domain before any matching rule runs; rule 1 (PROXY) then matches and, being earlier than rule 7, wins. A D here would mean sniffing did not feed domain rules.
No rule matches: pure route.final. Control case proving final flips between the two scenario configs.
